close_reason: Acknowledged. 'What is good' beads are decision/note observations — no code change required. They document good practices that the workspace already uses, retained for future reviewer reference if needed.
description: memory.rs:62-68 explicitly imports json_merge_patch from jmap-server and notes 'every reference backend imports it; the canonical RFC 7396 tests live with the function there (including the bd:JMAP-sc1b.97 depth-cap and bd:JMAP-sc1b.87 absent-field regression tests)'. This is the right call — a single shared merge-patch implementation across all 7 reference backends prevents the class of bug where one sibling diverges from another on patch semantics. The MergePatchError::DepthExceeded handling at memory.rs:677-682 maps cleanly to SetErrorType::InvalidPatch with a descriptive message. A future contributor might suggest 'just inline the merge-patch here for clarity' — the answer is no, the shared helper is doing real work.
title: What is good: explicit decision to use the foundation seam jmap_server::json_merge_patch for /set update — defends against silent regress
